correctness.rationale: For nonnegative three-periodic unilateral shift weights a,b,c, grouping residue coordinates bounds numerical radius by the Perron root of the half-weighted symmetric triangle; repeating its eigenvector across N periods proves the reverse bound, including zero weights. Writing L=2w, P=(S^2+Q)/3, R=abc gives L^3-PL-2R=0; the largest positive root increases strictly with R. Exact fixed-sum/fixed-second-moment minimization of abc yields the two-equal small-variance branch for q<1/2 and a zero-weight branch for q>=1/2, with all boundary equality cases. Rationalizing [F(q)-1/3]/q shows its minimum at q=1/2 and optimal linear stability coefficient 1/sqrt(2)-2/3. Independent NumPy diagonalization verified both lower bounds on 999 nonzero integer triples; this is corroboration only, not proof for every real triple.
